newsitem.title: LEBANON: More Lebanese arrive from Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: More Lebanese arrive from Sierra Leone.

text.p: A fourth group of Lebanese nationals arrived in Beirut on Thursday from Guinea after escaping a coup in Sierra Leone, an airport official said.
"A Middle East Airlines jumbo jet arrived from Conakry with 450 Lebanese men and women and 50 children," the official said.
Their arrival brought the number of Lebanese evacuees who returned home from Sierra Leone to 1,408 since last Thursday.
Lebanese officials say many Lebanese are still sheltering in the embassy in the Sierra Leone capital of Freetown.
Negotiations led by British and Nigerian diplomats to persuade leaders of the May 25 military coup to back down collapsed on Sunday.

Nigerian gunboats shelled the capital on Monday in a show of force aimed at reversing the coup. Rebels supporting the coup leaders responded by attacking Nigerian troops guarding foreigners at a hotel.

A truce was negotiated by the International Committee of the Red Cross and the city has been quiet since then. After a big U.S. evacuation on Tuesday, two French navy frigates evacuated 734 foreign nationals on Wednesday.
